title: Space Tech Briefing — October 16, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space cadets and cosmic enthusiasts! This is your daily dose of the latest from beyond our blue marble, live on October 16, 2026. Get ready to launch into the future with me!

First up, a monumental journey is nearing its climax! After an incredible eight-year odyssey, the BepiColombo mission is finally closing in on Mercury. This joint ESA-JAXA endeavor has traversed nearly 10 billion kilometers across the solar system, and the finish line is now in sight! Mark your calendars: BepiColombo is slated to enter orbit around the scorching hot planet Mercury on November 21st. What an achievement, bringing us closer than ever to understanding our solar system's innermost world!

Now, as we look ahead to these exciting new milestones, let's also take a moment to celebrate a recent triumph. We're still buzzing from the incredible achievements of French astronaut Sophie Adenot! Just a few days ago, on October 13th, she held her first press conference at the European Astronaut Centre in Cologne, following her return from the International Space Station. And what a mission it was! Sophie Adenot has set a new record for the longest stay in space by an ESA astronaut, spending an astonishing 237 days aboard the ISS. But that's not all! She's also the first ESA astronaut in two decades to complete three spacewalks on her very first mission. And, making history for her cohort, she's the first from ESA's Class of 2022 to have flown to space. Truly an inspiring performance!

And that's your cosmic update for this morning, October 16, 2026. Keep looking up, stay curious, and join us again tomorrow for more groundbreaking news from the final frontier. Have a stellar day!
